subject.title: fix: send managed Codex app-server version

question: Should OpenClaw’s Codex initialize identity always advertise the managed Codex compatibility version, including when a user configures a desktop or custom app-server command?
rationale: The dependency accepts a caller-defined client version and exposes it in backend-visible identity, but source alone cannot establish the intended OpenClaw product identity policy for non-managed commands.

options.title: Use compatibility identity everywhere
options.body: Treat the managed Codex train as OpenClaw’s declared client compatibility version for managed, desktop, and custom commands, with tests and documentation of that invariant.

options.title: Derive identity by command source
options.body: Use the managed compatibility version only for the managed package path and preserve or derive a different truthful identity for desktop and custom commands.

options.title: Keep the OpenClaw product version
options.body: Reject the identity change and pursue another fix after capturing the exact backend request and gate behavior.

recommendation.title: Use compatibility identity everywhere
recommendation.body: Treat the managed Codex train as OpenClaw’s declared client compatibility version for managed, desktop, and custom commands, with tests and documentation of that invariant.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history shows primary ownership of the app-server harness and its compatibility boundaries.
